D021-D005_h001.question: It's been... I'd say close to eight months now, maybe more, where things have just felt off. You know, I've always been pretty disciplined with my diet – you have to be in my line of work, staying sharp – but lately, it's become this all-consuming thing. I've cut out most carbs entirely, really watching the fats. My wife tries to get me to eat, but I just… I can't. It feels wrong, like it'll throw everything off. The weight has just been falling off, and honestly, I look at the scale multiple times a day, sometimes it feels like it’s taunting me. Even a slight fluctuation sends me into a spiral. I know it's not normal to be this fixated. Sometimes I feel like there are wires crossed in my head, like some subtle interference making me see and think things that don't quite fit with reality. It’s hard to explain, but it’s there, this nagging sense that something isn’t right in how I perceive things.
D021-D005_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h002.question: It's been… quite a while now, maybe a year or so, since things started feeling off. I’ve always been meticulous, especially with my work at the office, but it’s spread into everything. I’ve found myself becoming incredibly particular about what I eat, really limiting my intake. It’s not a diet, not exactly, but I just… I need to be in control. I've lost a fair amount of weight, and it keeps just shedding, despite my efforts to maintain some stability. The idea of gaining even a pound is, frankly, terrifying. I simply can't allow it. Sometimes, I feel like people are watching me, scrutinizing my choices, my plate. I know it sounds a bit odd, but I can't shake the feeling that certain individuals are trying to influence my eating habits, perhaps even poison my food to make me… bigger. It’s hard to explain, but I just know I need to be extra vigilant.
D021-D005_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h003.question: It’s been about six months now, maybe a little more, since I really started cutting back. I mostly just skip dinner, sometimes lunch too, if I’m not feeling up to it. I’ve lost a good bit of weight, which I guess is fine, but I just… I can’t stand the thought of gaining any back. It feels like if I let myself eat normally, everything will just unravel. I’ve been constantly looking for jobs, sending out applications, but it's hard to focus. Sometimes, I hear things, whispers really, that tell me I'm not good enough, or that people are watching me, judging what I eat. It's not constant, but it's unsettling, especially late at night when I'm alone in my apartment. I just want to feel normal again.
D021-D005_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h004.question: I’m not really sure why I’m here. My wife, Sarah, she’s been… worried. Says I’m not eating right. I tell her I’m just busy with work – breakthroughs in robotics don’t happen on a full stomach, you know? But then, sometimes I just forget to eat. Breakfast, lunch, dinner, it all just blurs. I’ve dropped a few pounds, sure, but it’s intentional. I prefer to keep my weight low; it keeps me sharp, optimized. I’ve always been a bit particular about what I put into my body. Like, I can’t eat pasta or bread, even a single piece of cake, I just know it’ll immediately translate to adipose tissue, slowing me down. Plus, there are certain… messages, I get. Frequencies, almost, guiding me on what to consume, what to avoid. They’re quite specific. They’ve been coming on and off for the past six months or so. Sometimes it feels like they’re trying to prevent me from being efficient.
D021-D005_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h005.question:
"Well, it's been a few months now, close to five, I think, since things started feeling... off. I've just not been hungry, you know? A bite or two of dinner, maybe some fruit during the day, that's usually all I can manage. My husband gets worried, but it’s just how it is. I’ve lost a noticeable amount of weight, which I suppose is part of it. I can't shake this intense dread of putting weight back on; the thought makes me feel utterly sick. Even a slight increase feels like a monumental failure.

And then there are these thoughts that just… intrude. Like, there’s this constant feeling that certain energies are trying to influence my designs at work, subtly altering my creative flow. I find myself meticulously reviewing every pixel, convinced there are hidden messages meant to sabotage my projects. It’s hard to explain, but it feels incredibly real, like someone or something is manipulating the very essence of my work. It’s exhausting, and it makes it hard to focus on anything else."
D021-D005_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D005_h006.question: "Well, doctor, it all started a few months after George passed. I just... lost my appetite, really. The thought of a full meal, especially anything with starches or fats, it just turns my stomach now. I try to stick to what’s healthy, you know, lean protein and vegetables. My daughter, bless her heart, she worries I’m too thin, but I tell her it’s just my metabolism at my age. I've always been a bit particular about what I eat, even during my nursing days, but it’s more pronounced now. Sometimes, it feels like certain foods are… sending messages, or trying to trick me. It’s hard to explain. When my GP mentioned putting on a few pounds, I just thought, 'He doesn't understand.' I feel perfectly fine, just a bit lighter, that's all. I know what's best for my body."
D021-D005_h006.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D005_h007.question: I’m not sure why I’m here. My husband, Mark, thinks something’s wrong because I’ve lost some weight and haven’t been eating much… honestly, I just don’t have much of an appetite these days. There’s so much going on with the restaurants, and I’m so busy. Skipping meals, especially lunch, just happens sometimes when there are a million things to do. Mark keeps mentioning that I look thin, but I think I look fine, maybe even a little heavy still. He says I’m dizzy sometimes, but it’s probably just because I’m on my feet all day. I overheard him telling his sister I think the government is trying to poison our food supply, which is ridiculous. It’s just that… sometimes I feel like certain batches of ingredients are “off”. But that’s just me being careful with quality control. This started… I guess about six months ago, more noticeably.
D021-D005_h007.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D005_h008.question: It’s hard to pinpoint when it started, but for about six months now, everything just feels… off. I’m only eating a few bites of food a day, sometimes just a small piece of toast or a few crackers. My boss at the cafe has noticed I’m looking thinner, but honestly, I think I could still stand to lose a bit more. People keep telling me I look pale and ask if I’m dizzy, but I just brush it off. What does it matter? They don’t understand that if I let myself gain weight, something terrible will happen. I’ve started noticing strange things too. Like, I’ll be serving a customer coffee, and I just know they’re talking about me behind my back, plotting something. Sometimes I see symbols in the steam from the espresso machine; they’re trying to tell me things, warn me. It’s all connected, I know it.
D021-D005_h008.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D005_h009.question: "It's been a tough few months, maybe even half a year now. My wife keeps hounding me about my eating, and the doctor too, but they just don't get it. I've cut right back on what I’m eating, pretty much the bare minimum. I’m quite strict with myself, you know? I feel better this way. They say I’m too thin, that I need to put on weight, but I don't see it. I feel… lighter, cleaner. They're making a fuss over nothing, honestly. Sometimes it feels like there's a reason for all of this, something they're missing, something I'm starting to understand. It’s hard to explain, but it feels important, very important, and connected to how I need to be."
D021-D005_h009.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D005_h010.question: "It's been a tough few months, doctor. I'm just… not myself. The numbers at work are always on my mind, even when I'm home. I've found myself becoming meticulous with what I eat, almost like an accounting ledger. I try to keep it to very little, just what I absolutely need to get through the day. My wife keeps saying I’m fading away, and I have to admit, the scale keeps dropping, but I tell her I'm fine. I feel perfectly healthy, just a bit tired sometimes. There’s no real problem. However, I can't shake this feeling that there are… signals… out there, trying to influence my decisions, especially around food. Sometimes I feel like I'm receiving instructions about how to manage my intake, like a secret code I need to decipher to keep everything in balance. It’s hard to talk about."
D021-D005_h010.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D021-D005_h011.question: It’s been a while since my wife passed, and things just haven’t been the same. I guess that’s when I really started watching what I eat, what little I do eat. My job as a night watchman doesn’t exactly help with a regular schedule, but honestly, I just don't feel like much. I keep to a very strict calorie count, barely anything at all, really. I tell myself it’s for my health, though, if I’m being honest, it feels more like a measure of my worth. The lighter I get, the better I feel about... well, everything. I’ve lost a lot of weight, continuously, and people have started noticing, but I just brush it off. Sometimes, I hear voices, soft at first, then more insistent, telling me that the food is poisoned, tainted somehow. It makes it even harder to eat, you know? They tell me to be careful, that I'm being watched, and the food is part of some larger plan.
D021-D005_h011.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h012.question:
I'm 42 and curating art used to be my whole world, but lately, it feels like everything is slipping. For about eight months now, the only thing I can think about is what I eat – or rather, what I *don't* eat. Half a rice cake for breakfast, a small salad for lunch… and that's usually it. I know I’m thin, my clothes hang off me, but every time I look in the mirror, I just see this softness, this extra weight, especially around my thighs and stomach. I just *have* to get it off.

My gallerist keeps telling me I'm too thin, that I need to eat more, but they just don't understand. They don't see what I see. Sometimes I worry they're all conspiring, trying to sabotage me, making me eat more so I lose my edge. I caught my assistant looking at me strangely the other day, and I just know she’s talking about me behind my back. It’s hard to trust anyone. I just need to be lighter, purer.
D021-D005_h012.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h013.question: It’s been a while since my husband passed, and honestly, the days just blur into one. I try to keep busy with the cleaning, but my appetite just isn't what it used to be. Most mornings, I skip breakfast. Lunch often just feels like too much effort, so I’ll pass on that too. I’ve definitely lost weight, and it's noticeable; my clothes are all loose now. Sometimes I think if I can just keep myself small, it means I’m doing something right, that I’m still a good person even after everything. It's like my worth is tied to how little space I take up. Lately, I've also been noticing things others don't, like coded messages in the dust motes telling me not to eat certain foods. It’s hard to explain, but it feels very real to me.
D021-D005_h013.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h014.question: "Honestly, Doc, things have been… off. Over the past few months, I’ve just lost my appetite. Dinner used to be a big deal, my wife makes great food, but now I’m barely touching it. A bite or two, sometimes just pushing it around my plate. The weight’s just been falling off me. My uniform feels looser every week, and my wife keeps commenting on it, asking if I’m sick. But I don't see it, well, not really anyway. When I look in the mirror, I still see a heavy guy, especially around the midsection. I’m not sure what to make of it. And then there are these… strange thoughts. Sometimes I feel like people are watching me, not just on the job, but everywhere, even when I’m home. Like there’s something they know that I don't, something about me they’re talking about."
D021-D005_h014.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h015.question:
I'm not sure what's going on, doc. It’s been a few months now, and I just… don’t feel right. Eating has become a real chore. I’ll take a few bites, maybe, throughout the day, but that’s about it. My weight keeps dropping, which is strange because I'm usually so on top of my macros and training. Honestly, it feels like my whole value as a person, especially in my line of work, hinges on how I look and how little I weigh. If I'm not perfectly lean, I feel like a complete failure.

It’s more than just the food though, there are these… thoughts. Sometimes I feel like people are watching me, especially when I’m eating or even just walking around. It’s hard to describe, but I get these strong feelings, like certain numbers or patterns are incredibly important, and if I don't follow them, something bad will happen. I know it sounds a bit out there, but they feel so real, so compelling. It's like I'm constantly on edge, trying to interpret all these subtle signs that only I seem to notice.
D021-D005_h015.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Bulimia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h016.question:
"Well, doctor, it's been a few months now, maybe five or six, since things started feeling off. My wife, bless her, keeps telling me I'm barely eating. I suppose she's right. I'll pick at my plate, maybe a bite or two, but then I just… lose interest. It’s strange, because I used to enjoy food. Now, the thought of certain things, especially anything a bit rich, just fills me with dread. It’s like, if I eat it, I’ll immediately balloon up. Even though, frankly, I know I'm already looking a bit gaunt. I'm a high school teacher, and I feel like I need to maintain a certain image, a certain… control.

And then there's the other stuff. Sometimes, I catch glimpses of things that aren't there, or hear whispers when no one's around. Nothing loud or insistent, just fleeting. It’s usually when I’m alone, often in the quiet of my classroom after the students have left. And I've been feeling like... someone is watching me, very closely, observing my every move. It’s hard to shake that feeling, even when I know it sounds a bit ridiculous. I just want to understand what's happening."
D021-D005_h016.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h017.question:
"It’s been rough lately, Doc. For about six months now, I just can't seem to eat right. A single bite or two is all I can manage for a meal, sometimes even just for a whole day. D021-D005_h017.options:

    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h018.question: It's been… I don't know, a few months now, maybe since the start of the semester, that things just feel off. I’m finding it really hard to eat much. I pick at my food, literally just a bite or two, and then I’m done. Sometimes I feel like I just can’t swallow it. I’m already so much thinner than I used to be, but I feel like I need to shed even more weight. I just get this overwhelming dread about certain foods, especially anything rich or high in calories. It’s like if I eat even a morsel of something like that, all my hard work will just… vanish, and I'll gain all the weight back instantly. It’s a very specific fear, almost like a certainty. Professor Miller was talking about the department needing "leaner operations" the other day, and I just kept thinking about how relevant that was to me, like a strange personal message. It’s hard to focus on my thesis with all this.
D021-D005_h018.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h019.question: "It's just… I can't seem to get a job, you know? And with that, I barely leave my apartment. Sometimes I feel like they're watching me, like the people online I've applied to are somehow connected, trying to keep me out. I barely eat, and I've lost a lot of weight these past few months, but honestly, it’s a good thing. I can't imagine gaining it back. The thought of it, of getting bigger, it fills me with dread. I just need to be lighter, less noticeable, and hopefully, then they'll stop… whatever they’re doing."
D021-D005_h019.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h020.question: "Honestly, doctor, it’s been a while now, maybe a year or so, that things started feeling... off. I just don't have the stomach for food like I used to. My wife, she tries, bless her heart, but even a single spoonful of her cooking feels like too much. I'll take a couple of bites, just to be polite, and that's it. D021-D005_h020.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa

    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizophrenia

D021-D005_h021.question: "Honestly, I'm doing great, better than ever. I've really dialed in my nutrition, keeping my calories super low to stay lean for my clients. D021-D005_h021.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D005_h022.question: It's been... I don't know, maybe six or seven months now, that I just don't feel like eating much. A bite or two of my wife's cooking is all I can manage most days. She worries, the kids too, but they just don't understand. I can't stand the thought of putting on weight, of becoming... *bloated*. I feel like people are watching me, judging my size. Even when the doctor tells me I'm too thin, that I need to eat more, he just doesn't get it. He thinks I'm making it up or something. He's probably part of some bigger plan, trying to make me fat so I can't do my job properly. I tell them all, "I'm fine, just not hungry," but they don't listen. They think I'm crazy. It’s like they’re trying to undermine me, get me to let down my guard. I just want to be left alone, to do my rounds at work. I need to be sharp.
D021-D005_h022.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D005_h023.question: “It’s been about six months now since things started feeling… off,” I begin, adjusting my glasses. “I’ve really cut back on what I’m eating. Just trying to be healthier, you know? At my age, an engineer needs to stay sharp. So, I’ve been keeping a close eye on the calories – nothing crazy, just being disciplined.” I pause, clearing my throat. “My wife, she worries, says I’m losing too much weight, but honestly, I feel fine. I check the scale every morning, sometimes twice, just to make sure I’m on track. A few grams up, and I get… uneasy. It’s important to maintain control, especially now. I know what’s going on, the signals, the way they transmit… if I don’t keep everything precise, the system could fail.” I shrug, a faint smile playing on my lips. “Doctors tend to overreact, always going on about this or that. I’m perfectly healthy. Just... optimizing.”
D021-D005_h023.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D005_h024.question:
"I'm here because… well, things haven't been right for a while.  It’s hard to pinpoint when it started, maybe six months ago, but it feels like a heavy weight. I’m just so swamped with work, the bankruptcy filings just pile up, and honestly, eating feels like another chore I can easily cut. I often skip breakfast entirely, and by lunchtime, I’m so focused on a brief that I just don’t bother. Dinner? Sometimes I manage a light salad, but I've been avoiding anything substantial for ages. High-calorie foods, in particular, just… they feel wrong, like they’ll instantly make me gain weight the moment they touch my lips.

I know I've lost weight, and sometimes I get dizzy spells, especially when I stand up too fast. My hair feels thinner, and my periods have been really irregular, almost nonexistent, but I try not to think about it too much. It just seems like a side effect of being so busy and under pressure. The thing is, I've also been having these intense thoughts lately. I've become convinced that there's a specific numerical code embedded in the legal documents I’m working on, and if I don't decipher it perfectly, the entire financial system will collapse. It sounds irrational, I know, but it feels incredibly real and urgent, consuming my every waking moment."
D021-D005_h024.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D005_h025.question:
